newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 3-yr yields close flat, CD yields fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 3-yr yields close flat, CD yields fall.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed flat on Monday as late profit-taking wiped out earlier falls in the yields, dealers said.
Three-month CD yields and the overnight call rate fell, helped by the central bank's plan to supply two trillion won into the money market, they said.
* 3-mth CDs end at 12.25 pct vs Saturday's 12.35 pct
* Average overnight call rate at 11.5 pct vs 11.8 pct
"There were also fears that the central bank would have no choice but to tighten money supply control after the Lunar New Year holiday," said a Hanjin Investment and Securities dealer.
Dealers said weak buying in corporate bonds issued by companies with relatively unstable financial positions was also a negative factor in corporate bond trading.
Hanbo Steel was declared insolvent after it defaulted on debt repayments on January 23. It is seeking court receivership.
The overnight call rate fell as cash liquidity remained high amid flexible money supply control by the central bank to prevent Hanbo's insolvency from causing a liquidity crunch.
